transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-10-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (CTO - Pegasus Retail), Maya Lin (Lead ML Eng), Evan Cole (Infra Lead)

Auto Summary: quick intro, qualification (stack, timeline), demo request for self-serve quickstart, security questions (SOC2/SSO/KMS), next steps to provision credits and run benchmarks.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin, i'm alex from redwood, samir is our se, and then over to you folks for quick intros
[00:12] Jordan (CTO): jordan here, running platform at pegasus, we own the checkout search and personalization services, looking into adding some LLM features for product rec and merch ops
[00:25] Maya (ML): maya — lead on ml, mostly responsible for model evaluation and infra cost analysis, excited to see the ttft (time to first token) and cost numbers
[00:38] Evan (Infra): evan, infra lead, i'll be focused on network/VPC options and how we can keep data in our cloud account
[00:48] Samir (SE): great, thanks. high level — today we want to map quick wins: self-serve flow, free credits, how long to get a first API call, and then larger options — dedicated pools or private vpc for production

[01:15] Jordan: timeline wise, we want a funcional prototype in two weeks and a pilot by end of quarter. so ttft is important. can you do zero to first call in under a day for our engineers?
[01:30] Alex: yes, that's our bread and butter for plg. we usually provision credits and a quickstart repo. typical path: sign up, get api key, run sample curl or sdk script, first call within an hour if infra isn't blocked. sometimes identity teams slow it down.
[01:49] Maya: any common friction points? like do we need network peering or anything for hosted quickstarts?
[01:56] Samir: for hosted it's straight — no peering. you call our endpoint over TLS. for dedicated or private, you can do VPC peering or bring-your-own-vnet, which takes extra setup (we'll need your cloud team and a small ipsec/vpn window).

[02:20] Evan: ok that's good. on security — we need to see SOC2, log retention, SSO integration (SAML/Okta), and KMS support for keys. are those available for self-serve?
[02:33] Alex: yes SOC2 is public, we can share the audit summary. SSO is available on paid tiers, but we also support API keys for plg. KMS encryption at rest is supported on Dedicated/Private — hosted has envelope encryption with our managed keys, but we can discuss bring-your-own-key for enterprise / private installs.
[02:50] Jordan: and data residency? some of our logs must stay in eu region, we are mostly us-east but have eu customers
[02:58] Samir: we have region pinned endpoints and you can choose region for hosted — we also have Dedicated pools in eu-west for enterprise commitments. Private deployment gives you full residency since control plane is in your vpc.

[03:20] Maya: for the quickstart, what models are available? we want embedders and a smaller generation model for reranking recommendations
[03:28] Samir: we expose a model catalog, embeddings, chat/generation, and reranking tools. typical quickstart uses a 7b open model for cheaper prototyping and you can switch to optimized variants. we also provide perf profiles per model so you can estimate token cost and latency.
[03:45] Alex: and our optimize tool will suggest quantization and batching settings based on your request pattern — that helps reduce unit cost once you hit volume.

[04:05] Jordan: curious about latency numbers — rough ballpark p95 for a 1k token generation on hosted vs dedicated?
[04:12] Samir: hosted p95 for 1k tokens on a 7b-type model is typically 300-500ms per token for streamed responses depends on concurrency, but for short responses it's the model init and token decode. Dedicated with GPUs and our optimized kernels can push p95 lower — say 200-350ms depending on batch strategy and KV caching. these numbers are noisy, we recommend running your own sample through our quick benchmark.
[04:38] Maya: okay, that delta matters — cost wise do you see big unit savings on dedicated?
[04:44] Samir: yes. dedicated reserved pools reduce per-token cost by around 30-60% depending on utilization and model. autoscaling and burst policy matter here.

[05:05] Evan: we will likely want to test both routes: quick hosted proof-of-concept to validate feature, then a dedicated pilot for predictable throughput and cost. question on canary/fallbacks — if a dedicated pool is saturated do you have automatic fallback to hosted?
[05:18] Alex: absolutely. we have routing policies: failover to hosted or to a smaller quantized variant. you can configure fallbacks per route.

[05:35] Jordan: operationally, what do devs need to run the quickstart? is there a curl example and sdk?
[05:41] Samir: yes, we have curl, python node sdks, and a postman collection. the quickstart includes sample prompts, small dataset loaders for embeddings, and a benchmark spreadsheet.

[06:00] (background): paper rustle, crosstalk

[06:10] Maya: transcription note — i wanted to ask about kv cache and prefix caching, does that come out of the box?
[06:17] Samir: yes prefix/KV caching is automatic at the runtime level — it helps chat flows a lot. our runtime retains per-session kv cache for a configurable ttl. note: caching affects consistency so we document invalidation patterns.

[06:40] Jordan: there's also some regulatory stuff — we need audit logs and the ability to pull logs for specific requests for compliance.
[06:47] Alex: audit logs are available on Dedicated/Private with longer retention. hosted has standard logs, you can export to your SIEM. we'll include the retention table in the security packet.

[07:05] Maya: can we run embeddings locally against our product catalog, any privacy gotchas?
[07:12] Samir: hosted embeddings send data to the service; if you need the embeddings to remain in your VPC, Private or Dedicated with private networking is the way. For many customers a hosted contractual NDA and retention controls are fine for POCs, but we will document the differences.

[07:35] Jordan: what about billing and credits? we want to give our product team 30 days of experimentation without procurement overhead
[07:42] Alex: we can provision 30-day trial credits to your account and give your devs a single API key scoped to the project. they'll see token usage in the console. after the credits expire you can convert to a pay-as-you-go or start a reserved capacity contract.

[08:00] Evan: if we spin up a private deployment, how long does the onboarding take? we're thinking air-gapped options for compliance later
[08:08] Samir: Private on-prem install depends on your environment but typical timeline is 4–8 weeks with our private deployment team. For VPC-hosted private control plane it can be 2–4 weeks. air-gapped on-prem is the longest due to network and security reviews.

[08:30] Jordan: good. let's talk benchmarks — what's the lightest touch to get meaningful numbers?
[08:36] Samir: run 1k representative requests against the quickstart endpoint (both embeddings and chat) and capture p50/p95 token latency and per-token costs. we provide a small benchmark harness in the repo.

[09:00] Maya: we'll do that, but need to know what to expect for results format. do you provide a template?
[09:07] Alex: yes we'll attach a spreadsheet with columns: model, endpoint, concurrency, p50/p95 lat, tokens per call, total cost estimate, notes. we'll also share a sample run we did for a retailer.

[09:25] Jordan: are there any gotchas with our stack — we run services on aws (us-east), kubernetes EKS for microservices, and use Okta for SSO.
[09:33] Samir: that's common. for SSO you'll want SAML config which is on paid tiers. EKS doesn't affect the quickstart for hosted. For dedicated we can provision a private network that peers with your VPC and your infra team will set the allowed CIDRs.

[09:55] Evan: wondering about routing and per-route quotas, we expect spikes at 10–20 qps per service during promos, need autoscale.
[10:03] Samir: you can configure per-route SLOs and autoscale policies; dedicated pools support predictable throughput and configurable burst capacity.

[10:18] (small laugh)

[10:25] Alex: ok before we wrap, quick recap: we will provision credits, send quickstart repo + postman, and share security docs (SOC2 and SAML notes). customer will run smoke tests and schedule a deep-dive on private/vpc options.

[10:45] Maya: that aligns. i also want the benchmark template and a small sample that mirrors retail search re-ranking (50–200 tokens typical).
[10:55] Alex: noted, we'll include that.

[11:05] Jordan: one more question — do you have an example of a canary rollout or A/B config in your console? our product team wants to do slow ramp on a small percentage of traffic
[11:15] Samir: yes our console supports canary % rollouts and fallback policies across model variants and regions. we also emit traces so you can tie model responses back to requests in your logs.

[11:34] Evan: thanks, sounds good. we'll aim to have the smoke test results in a week.

[11:42] Alex: perfect. we'll send notes and credits today. thanks everyone.

[11:50] (meeting ends)

Recap / Next Steps:
- Redwood to provision 30-day credits and quickstart materials (Alex)
- Customer to run 1k-request smoke benchmark (Maya)
- Schedule infra deep-dive for private/VPC options (Samir + Evan)
- Redwood to share SOC2 summary, SAML integration notes, and retention table (Alex)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and filler words; some technical terms spelled phonetically (kv cache sometimes transcribed as "k-v cash"), product names sometimes abbreviated.
